entities.name: PMID:28874935
observations: US privately insured and Medicare Advantage ED visits, 2005–2013: 33.1 million visits; 17.8% involved CT, and ED CT use increased 59.9%.
Increase occurred across age groups, although pediatric ED CT decreased after 2010.

entities.name: PMID:23683773
observations: US NHAMCS and Ontario data, 2003–2008: ED visits involving CT increased faster in the US than Ontario; all subgroups increased except Ontario children under 10.
US ED CT use was 11.4% of visits versus 5.9% in Ontario.

entities.name: PMID:24080717
observations: Integrated US practice population, 2000–2010: overall CT utilization rose only 10% (178.5 to 195.9 scans per 1,000 patients), while ED CT rose 81% (41.1 to 74.4 per 1,000).
Authors characterized overall utilization as stable across the decade while ED CT increased substantially.

entities.name: PMID:22331345
observations: Two tertiary pediatric EDs, 2003–2010: no overall change in CT utilization; head CT declined for seizure and head injury, while abdominal ultrasound increased for abdominal pain.

entities.name: PMID:31339541
observations: US pregnancy cohorts, 1996–2016: CT rose 3.7-fold overall, but US CT rates stabilized through 2010 and declined by 2016; radiography also declined after an early increase, while MRI rose steadily.

entities.name: ED imaging growth exceeds overall CT growth

relations.to: ED imaging growth exceeds overall CT growth
